text:
maria: Heads up — CI eval for the new q4f16 bring-up is nondeterministic. Locally I run the eval 10x and outputs (and pass@1) are identical, in CI the same job retried 3 times produced different sampled completions.

kevin: Can you paste the CI run ids and a couple of differing outputs? :eyes:

maria: Sure — job 6821 (docker: inference:v2026-03), retries 1/2/3. Example snippet from the same prompt:
```
# retry 1 (seed 42 in logs)
Prediction: "The cat sat on the mat."
# retry 2 (seed 42 in logs)
Prediction: "The cat sits on the couch."
```
Logs show SEED=42 set at start for the runner.

sam: That smells like environment or process-level nondeterminism — ordering of RNG init (python random -> numpy -> torch) or something platform-specific. CI image differs from your local container?

ci-bot: job 6821 metadata: image=inference:v2026-03, ubuntu:22.04, python=3.10.13, numpy=1.23.5, tokenizers=0.13.3

natalie: I spun up the same image locally and reproduced the divergence inside a container when LANG was unset. When I force LANG=en_US.UTF-8 the runs become stable. When LANG=C.UTF-8 the tokenizer sometimes yields different internal hash iteration order affecting dict traversal in our legacy postproc.

alex: Also noticed CI installs numpy from cache (1.23) while local env uses 1.25. Small numpy RNG/algorithm changes could change intermediate sampling noise and interact with top_p rounding.

maria: Minimal repro I used inside the container:
```
import random, numpy as np, torch
random.seed(42)
np.random.seed(42)
torch.manual_seed(42)
# run tokenization + sampling pipeline
```
Even with that order, if PYTHONHASHSEED is not set and locale differs we get different dict traversal in postprocessing, which shifts a few top_p votes.

sam: Plan: 1) standardize seed initialization in the runner (explicit wrapper that seeds random, np, torch, and sets PYTHONHASHSEED), 2) pin locale and enforce LANG in Dockerfile, 3) add token-id checksum telemetry and assert in CI smoke.

rachel: I'll add telemetry metric: token_ids_checksum and sample_entropy so CI can diff numbers across retries. Also add a short assertion in the CI job that for deterministic smoke (matrix job) the checksum must match. If mismatch, fail the job early and upload the three outputs.

kevin: Can we also pin numpy minor version for the short term and add a flaky-bisect job that reruns the failing eval under a set of env variants? That will help isolate whether locale vs numpy vs seed order.

maria: Assigning: natalie -> Dockerfile locale + numpy pin update and new image build; sam -> seed-wrapper + PYTHONHASHSEED env and add unit to runner init; rachel -> telemetry + CI assertion. I'll open a P1 issue and attach the CI job ids. :white_check_mark:

alex: One more thing — add the seed value captured in telemetry for every eval invocation and the exact versions of tokenizers and tokenization config (vocab checksum). That made prior flake hunts much faster.

maria: Agreed. I'll update the eval harness PR with telemetry fields and a small reproducer script to include in tools/ so infra can run the deterministic smoke locally.

kevin: Nice. If anyone hits this again tag me. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: linked issue opened: #4127 — "CI-only RNG/locale nondeterminism in eval runner" (owner: maria)
